adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb line 22: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`. This accepts any client-provided limit value without an upper bound check. A malicious client could pass limit=1000000 to force the server to load and serialize an arbitrarily large number of users in a single request, potentially causing performance issues or denial of service. This is a real security/performance issue - there's no maximum cap on the limit parameter, only a default of 50 if not provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — P1 confidence 100: `render json: { members: serialize_data(members, GroupUserSerializer), meta: { total: total, limit: limit, offset: offset } }` silently changes the existing `/groups/:group_id/members` response contract from a top-level member array to an object, breaking existing clients and plugins that deserialize or iterate the documented-by-behavior array shape without any versioned endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows a change in the response format of the `/groups/:group_id/members` endpoint. The old code used `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` which returns a top-level array of members. The new code returns `render json: { members: serialize_data(members, GroupUserSerializer), meta: { total: total, limit: limit, offset: offset } }` which wraps the members in an object with 'members' and 'meta' keys. This is a breaking API change that would affect any existing clients or plugins that expect the array format. The corresponding JavaScript changes in the diff (e.g., `result.members.map(...)` and `result.meta.total`) confirm this is an intentional structural change. This is a real backward compatibility issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — P1, confidence 100: `group.users.delete(user_id)` passes an Integer to ActiveRecord's collection `delete`, which requires `User` records and raises `ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch`, so the remove-member endpoint cannot complete.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb at line 90, the code is `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i`. The `delete` method on an ActiveRecord association (has_many :users) expects either record objects or record IDs. According to Rails documentation, `collection.delete(object, ...)` removes objects from the collection by setting their foreign keys to NULL or deleting them. However, when passing an integer ID directly to `delete` on a has_many association, Rails actually does accept IDs - it will find and delete records with those IDs. The finding claims this raises `ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch`, but this is incorrect. Rails' `delete` method on associations can accept IDs as integers. The code should work correctly.
